text:
Maria: proposing a mixed-capacity pool design for GPU fleets — min on-demand floor + spot/preemptible burst pool. Want design feedback on composition, interruption handling, and rollout constraints. Quick sketch: default on-demand floor = 20% of regional GPU capacity; burst spot pool up to 70% with an enforced min hot-spare per AZ; scheduler should prefer spot for stateless / fast-warm models. Also need graceful preemption flow and metrics to avoid SLO regressions.

Aj: +1 on trying this. Clarify: is the 20% floor per region or global? also how do we handle capacity reservations for enterprise customers?

Maria: per-region by default (we can override per-customer). reservations = map to on-demand only or dedicated capacity. For customers with reserved SLAs we'll pin to dedicated/on-demand. The floor protects latency-sensitive traffic.

Sourav: big concern = AZ/rack blast radius with spot. If all spot instances come from the same instance type / AZ, preemption hits many replicas. Recommend: enforce AZ diversity and prefer multiple instance families in the spot pool. Autoscaler needs to consider 'spread' constraint.

Tanya: interruption handling proposal: preemption webhook -> mark node "DRaining-spot" -> scheduler stops placing new work -> try graceful checkpointing within N=30s (model-dependent) -> if checkpoint fails, fallback route sends requests to on-demand pool and serve degraded (lower concurrency) until warm cache rebuild. Also keep a tiny hot spare pool (2-3 nodes per AZ) to absorb immediate failover.

Ben: cost model quick note: with 20% on-demand floor and average spot discount 60%, we estimate ~35% savings vs all on-demand for typical workload mix. But if spot interruption rate > 15% in a region, savings fall below 20% when factoring extra egress and rewarm costs. Need region-by-region sims and tail-latency impact.

Kevin: scheduler changes: introduce weighted bin-packing with preference score = f(model_statefulness, warmup_cost, latency_slo, spot_score). For stateless or cheap-warm models, score favors spot. For large models with long KV warmup, prefer on-demand or prewarmed spot nodes. Also add network-awareness: avoid packing cross-rack egress-heavy replicas on spot nodes in different AZs to reduce VPC egress costs.

deploy-bot: created ticket INFRA-7892 for "mixed pool rollout pilot" and added community watcher.

Maria: action items: (1) Aj + Sourav: prototype AZ spread + autoscaler changes, run failure drills in staging; (2) Tanya: implement preemption handler + 30s checkpoint hook and hot-spare keeper; (3) Ben: run cost sims per-region and interruption-sensitivity matrix; (4) Kevin: extend scheduler scoring heuristics and add telemetry hooks for warmup time. target: pilot in us-west-2 next week.

Aj: I'll take (1). I'll add telemetry: interruption_rate, fallback_routing_rate, fallback_latency, and KV-warmup-time.

Ben: I'll run sims and post a short spreadsheet with assumptions by EOD. :thumbsup:

Sourav: adding a note — make sure we don't overcommit spot IPs in our VPC nat gateways; if many spot nodes boot at once we can saturate SNAT. Will add NAT usage check to the autoscaler preflight.

Kevin: I'll implement scheduler changes in the feature branch and include a toggle for pilot. We should also add a canary that keeps 3% of traffic on all-on-demand to detect regressions early.

Maria: perfect. let's sync tomorrow 10am for rollout checklist. thanks all! :rocket:
